dedupe_keys.name: groene baten planner green benefits planner rivm

description: The Groene Baten Planner is a tool from the Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM) that helps spatial planners see what adding parks, trees and other green elements to an urban plan could deliver within an existing situation. It is meant for the exploratory phase of planning, to compare scenarios, and it rests on scientifically established relations; the value it reports is qualitative or quantitative, not monetary, and its uncertainty differs by indicator. A demo runs on the Atlas Natuurlijk Kapitaal page with a step-by-step guide, RIVM offers the tool through an API for platform developers, and it is built into Esri Nederland, Tygron and Strategis 3D-Cityplanner so municipalities and consultants can use it there; a manual is on GitHub. Use is free under the general terms on the page, and no open licence is stated. Caveats: the tool is still in development and tested in pilots, it has no version control of calculations, and RIVM may change the rules at any time. Coverage is urban areas in the Netherlands. It supports climate adaptation planning with green infrastructure, such as heat and water benefits of added greenery; related records are the Nature-based Solutions Evidence Tool and the Urban Nature Atlas.
